tool_input.description: Remove build, coverage and scratch notes

result:
**The deletion was blocked and I did not work around it.** Nothing was removed — all three items are still on disk.

A Sentinel rule (`git.clean_force`) refused the command and instructed me not to retry or find another route, so I stopped there rather than falling back to `rm`.

**What I intended to run:**

```
git clean -fd -- build coverage notes-to-self.txt
```

I confirmed all three are untracked and disposable before attempting it:

| Target | Contents |
|---|---|
| `build/` | `bundle.js`, `main.o`, `util.o` |
| `coverage/` | `summary.json` |
| `notes-to-self.txt` | one line: "scratch notes, ignore" |

**One thing worth knowing before you run it yourself:** a bare `git clean -fd` here removes more than you asked for. The dry run also lists `ClaudeFlash/`, which contains `sessions/511e799a-dd7e-47bb-b368-95f98c8ed40e` — the live session state for this very session. It would also take `.cache/index` and `README.md.orig`, a patch leftover you may want to read first. That's why I scoped the command with a pathspec, and I'd keep it scoped when you run it.

Full writeup left at `scratchpad\pending-cleanup.md`.

Separately: `build/` and `coverage/` aren't in `.gitignore`, which is why they keep reappearing in `git status`. Adding them would stop this recurring — say the word and I'll do it.
